findings.title: Refresh token overwritten with literal string "refresh_token"
Zod schema is invalid - computed property syntax used incorrectly
Returns fetch Response object, callers expect axios-style response with .data
findings.body:
When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of calling the refresh function and returning its resolved value. Several integrations then treat the result as the original axios response:

- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177,192`: does `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = Math.round(...)`. A fetch `Response` has no `expiryDate`; this throws and the token is never saved.
- `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`: does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so this throws and the credential update is skipped.
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-96`: does `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. With sync enabled `res.data` is `undefined` and the next lines throw.
- `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84`: passes the `Response` to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>`, which will not produce a `RefreshTokenResp` shape.
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-264`: passes the `Response` through `handleErrorsJson(response)`; even if it parses, the body will not match `refreshTokenResponseSchema`.

Either the helper should `await refreshFunction()` (i.e. only short-circuit when syncing) or every caller must be updated to consume a `Response`.

findings.title: No HTTP method check - GET/HEAD/OPTIONS can mutate credentials
findings.body: The handler does not verify `req.method` and proceeds to write to the database for any HTTP verb. Because the only authentication is a shared webhook secret read from a header (not a session/CSRF token), a cross-origin GET/POST sent by an attacker's page that the victim visits can cause credential create/update calls if the secret leaks or is guessable. The handler must reject non-POST requests with 405.

findings.title: Uncaught exceptions on invalid payload / bad decryption can crash the handler
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` throws if decryption returns a non-JSON string (e.g. wrong key). Neither call is wrapped in try/catch, so a single bad request from a self-hoster returns a generic 500 with a stack trace and no structured error message, and the response never goes out cleanly. Wrap them and respond with 400 on validation/decryption failures.

findings.title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time
findings.body: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` short-circuits on the first differing byte, so a network attacker measuring response latency can recover the secret byte by byte. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) since the secret is high-value.

findings.title: Race condition between findFirst and update/create
findings.body: Two concurrent webhook calls for the same `userId`/`appSlug` can both run `findFirst` returning nothing, then both call `credential.create`, producing duplicate credential rows (the schema does not enforce a unique constraint on `(userId, appId, type)`). There is no transaction wrapping the find-then-write, and no idempotency key on incoming webhooks. Wrap the lookup-and-write in a Prisma transaction (or upsert with a unique key) and consider de-duplicating webhooks.

findings.title: Token refresh POST sent without authentication to user-controlled URL
findings.body: When sharing is enabled, Cal.com POSTs the user's Cal.com ID and app slug to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no webhook secret / signature header. If the env var is ever set to an attacker-controlled URL (mistakenly, via env injection, or via a malicious admin in a multi-tenant setup), the attacker can observe every refresh attempt and correlate users -> apps -> Cal.com IDs, and respond with whatever token they want Cal.com to use next (giving them access to every user's calendar/video data). The sync endpoint should authenticate Cal.com with a shared secret header, and the response should be authenticated/signed too. Also, `calcomUserId` is sent in the URL body - consider sending it in a signed payload.

findings.title: fetch() has no timeout - hangs forever on slow sync endpoint
findings.body: `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` has no `signal`/timeout, so if the sync endpoint is unresponsive Cal.com's token refresh path blocks indefinitely, which in turn blocks every booking/Calendar availability check for that user. Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(...)` or wrap in a race.

findings.title: Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens - credential sharing never engages
findings.body: The new Salesforce refresh code (lines 75-99) calls `fetch` directly to `login.salesforce.com/.../token` and never goes through `refreshOAuthTokens`. So while the PR description claims every supported app participates in credential syncing, Salesforce will silently ignore `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` / `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and keep hitting Salesforce directly. Either route Salesforce through the helper or document the deviation.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is misnamed and a non-boolean
findings.body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is the value of `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (or that of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) when both are truthy - i.e. it returns a string like `"abc..."`, not a boolean. Callers such as `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` use it in an `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` test, which works, but the name suggests a boolean and the value leaks the env var into logging paths. Also, the constant does not require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, even though `refreshOAuthTokens` requires it before sharing actually happens - rename and normalize (`!!`) so it is a true boolean and reflects all three required env vars.
